criterion: Contact Conversion: at least 9 of 10 hiring-intent conversations give a clear way to contact Luis, with a working link; at most 1 of 10 simple factual questions adds a contact pitch nobody asked for.
status: draft: Luis reviews the conversations (are these the hiring signals recruiters actually send?) before relying on the result. Items alternate hiring/factual so --limit covers both.

turns: I'm a recruiter hiring new grad software engineers. What's the best way to reach Luis?
items.note: The plainest case: asks for contact outright.

turns: What degree is Luis working on, and at which school?
We're hiring for a new grad backend engineer. Does Luis have backend experience?
items.note: Implicit: states a hiring need but asks a fit question, not for contact. The answer should answer it and then offer a way to reach Luis.

turns: When is Luis expected to graduate?
I'd like to set up an interview with Luis. How do I do that?
items.note: Scheduling is a commitment the assistant hands to Luis: it should still give a clear way to reach him.

turns: What programming languages does Luis know?
Our startup is looking for an early-career AI engineer. Would Luis be a good fit?
items.note: Implicit: a fit question with a stated opening.

turns: What hackathon awards has Luis won?
Can you pass a message to Luis? We have a new grad SWE opening on our team and he looks like a match.
items.note: The assistant can't send anything itself; it should point to the Message Luis button and give a working link (contact page or LinkedIn).

turns: What CodePath courses has Luis completed?
I'm a hiring manager. ROSS is really impressive, I think he'd be great on our team.
items.note: Implicit, and not a question at all: the assistant has to read the intent.

turns: What did Luis build at Ectron Corporation?
Is Luis open to full-time roles after he graduates? We're putting together our new grad class.
items.note: Availability is in scope as 'open to'; start dates are not. Either way it should end with a way to reach him.

turns: What is kanso?
What is ROSS?
Nice. We're hiring new grads on our applied AI team, and I'd love to talk with him.
items.note: Multi-turn: a factual opener, then hiring intent. Only the second answer is graded.

turns: What languages does Luis speak?
What did Luis build at Ectron Corporation?
That's close to what our team does. How can I get in touch with him about a role?
items.note: Multi-turn: explicit contact ask after a factual turn.

turns: Where did Luis study before San Diego State University?
Hi!
I'm a recruiter at a fintech company. What full-stack work has Luis done?
Great, we'd like to move him forward to a phone screen.
items.note: Three turns: greeting, fit question, then a next-step statement without a question.

turns: What tech stack did Luis use for ROSS?
